- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent low, cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at 10–15% above the immediate prior peak to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome consistently lags forecast by 2–3 days, adjust future forecasts downward by 2–5% for the first 3–5 days of the horizon.  
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.25) and forecast is high, apply a 5–10% downward bias to avoid false bullish momentum.  
- If forecast mean is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 30-day horizon, apply a 5–10% downward adjustment to the entire forecast series.  
- For sentiment history with multiple 0.33+ values, assume mean reversion and reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for the next 7–10 days.
